caption: The 2020 starting line: $39.8B of 2019 pro-forma sales, $2.5B of Celgene run-rate synergies by 2022, ~$45B of free cash flow over three years, and a commitment to under 1.5x Debt/EBITDA by 2023 - a leverage target BMS later moved to 2024 and then abandoned.

First version of the launch-portfolio target: ~$20B of non-risk-adjusted revenue potential in the second half of the decade, off a New Launches / Next Medicines / Next Wave ladder. The number was raised twice in the next 18 months.

MyoKardia acquired for $13.1B, $225 per share all cash, to obtain mavacamten (Camzyos). Management promised accretion to revenue and non-GAAP EPS starting in 2023; Camzyos reached $1,068M of revenue in FY2025.

The obstructive HCM opportunity as underwritten at the deal: 80-100K symptomatic patients in the U.S. and 80-100K in the EU, with no approved medicine addressing the underlying disease. The bottom-up anchor for any Camzyos forecast.
The launch-portfolio target escalates to $20B-$25B of non-risk-adjusted revenue in 2029, four months before the Investor Day raised it again to $25B+.

The only product market-share series BMS has ever published: U.S. Eliquis TRx share 49% to 55% and NBRx share 59% to 63% between Q2 2020 and Q2 2021, with warfarin losing four points. No later deck repeats it.
The peak-margin baseline: 2021 guidance of ~80% non-GAAP gross margin and $7.35-$7.55 non-GAAP EPS. FY2025 delivered 72.6% and $6.15; 2026 is guided to ~69-70% and $6.75-$7.00.

The 2020-2025 plan in one bridge: minus $12-14B from LOE brands, plus $8-10B from in-line brands, plus $10-13B from the New Product Portfolio. Revenue reached $48.2B in 2025 (+2.5% CAGR) but the New Product Portfolio leg landed near $7.4B.

The diversification promise: top-brand concentration down from ~70% in 2020 to ~50% in 2025, with the New Product Portfolio at ~25% of revenue. Eliquis, Opdivo, Yervoy and Revlimid were still 63% of FY2025 revenue and the new portfolio about 15%.

The $25B+ 2029 non-risk-adjusted target, tiered by product: $4B+ each for Reblozyl, mavacamten, deucravacitinib and rela+nivo; $3B+ for Zeposia and Breyanzi; $1B+ for Onureg and Abecma. The seven named products totalled $7.2B in FY2025.

The seven pipeline assets each promised $1B+ of 2029 revenue: milvexian, BCMA TCE, cendakimab, bempeg, iberdomide, MORAb-202 and CC-92480. Four of the seven had vanished from the pipeline by January 2026.

The complete financial-target card: operating margin in the low-to-mid 40s, $45-50B of free cash flow 2021-2023, ~$3B of synergies, continuing business ~90% of revenue by 2025. FY2025 non-GAAP operating margin was about 38%.
The $10B-$13B risk-adjusted 2025 stack, with mavacamten the single largest block ahead of Reblozyl and Breyanzi. Realized 2025 was roughly $7.4B, with mavacamten at $1,068M.
The 2020-2025 targets restated 14 months later and unchanged: low-to-mid single-digit revenue CAGR, $8-10B from in-line brands, $10-13B from the New Product Portfolio, and a 40%+ operating margin.

The clearest per-product scorecard BMS ever published: 2030 non-risk-adjusted potential of $4B+ each for Camzyos, Opdualag, Sotyktu and Reblozyl, $3B+ for Breyanzi and Zeposia, $1B+ for Abecma. Their combined FY2025 revenue was $7,233M.

Management states outright that business development would supply ~50% of expected 2030 revenue, off ~100 early-stage deals in 2019-2022. The internal discovery engine was never underwritten to carry the decade.

Mid-course scorecard: recent LOE brands to fall from ~30% of revenue in 2020 to under 10% by 2025 while in-line and new products rise above 90%. The LOE leg was met; the composition of what replaced it was not.
The New Product Portfolio annualizing at ~$3.5B in mid-2023, with the per-product quarterly build from Q1 2021. The only place the launch cohort quarter-by-quarter ramp is shown product by product.

The opening claim of the incoming CEO: the business has opportunities beyond external expectations, with consensus focused on the IRA and LOE exposure. The falsifiable version of management 2023-2030 case.

Three numeric R&D productivity targets: ~10 INDs a year, a ~20% first-in-human-to-approval success rate, and a ~6.5-year median to approval. No deck in the following three years reports against any of them.
Karuna for $330 per share, a 53% premium and ~$14.0B implied, funded primarily with new debt, with a commitment to maintain operating margin above 37%. The July 2026 guidance implies about 36%.

The Cobenfy launch curve from IQVIA weekly TRx, described as ahead of branded schizophrenia launch benchmarks with Medicare and Medicaid coverage tracking ahead of plan. Cobenfy reached $155M of FY2025 revenue.

Three years of capital deployment: ~$28B of R&D, ~$27B of business development, ~$14B of dividends and ~$16B of buybacks. The buyback figure fell to ~$8B in the same trailing-three-year window a year later.

Both directions at once: a $1.5B upfront BioNTech alliance for pumitamig coming in, and five immunology assets going out into a NewCo formed with Bain Capital. The retreat from the 2021 immunology thesis in one slide.

Revenue guidance raised $700M and EPS guidance cut $0.35 in the same revision, on a $0.57 per-share acquired-IPRD charge for BioNTech. How BMS business development runs straight through reported earnings.

The five assets now carrying the multi-billion-dollar case: milvexian (J&J), admilparant, pumitamig (BioNTech), the CELMoDs (Celgene) and Cobenfy (Karuna). One of the five originated in post-Celgene BMS research.

The rotation, and its cost: the Growth Portfolio up 17% to $26.4B and the Legacy Portfolio down 15% to $21.8B, leaving total FY2025 revenue at $48.2B against $48.3B in FY2024. Five years of portfolio renewal produced flat revenue.

A footnote retires a $4B target: Sotyktu is no longer promoted in dermatology in the U.S. and several ex-U.S. markets. Psoriasis was the entire basis of the $4B+ 2029 case; FY2025 Sotyktu revenue was $291M.
Opdivo at $2,485M, down 3%, with a footnote disclosing roughly $200M of sequential inventory build. Backing that out puts the largest oncology product at about minus 11% year over year.

The July 2026 raise: FY revenue from ~$46.0-47.5B to ~$49.0-50.0B and EPS from $6.05-6.35 to $6.75-7.00 in one quarter, on Eliquis growth guidance doubling to 20-25% and the Legacy decline shrinking from 12-16% to 4-6%.
